Host Ollie breaks down the latest data from NOAA, NASA, and ESA into plain English for aurora chasers, ham radio operators, satellite operators, and anyone curious about what the Sun is doing today.

item.title: Roman Telescope Weekend Launch & Asteroid 2025 UK9 Flyby
item.description:
In today's episode of the Daily Space Podcast by Flarient, Ollie breaks down the latest live space weather conditions and major astronomical headlines for Friday, September 4, 2026.
We start with a complete look at today's exceptionally tranquil space weather report. With the Kp index sitting at a calm 0 to 0.33 and solar wind speeds holding steady at 412.8 kilometres per second, Earth's magnetosphere is experiencing minimal pressure. We discuss what these numbers mean for satellite operators, power grid managers, and aurora chasers.
Next, we dive into four deep-dive articles from the Flarient blog. We explore the composition of the interstellar medium, learning how diffuse gas and interstellar grains act as raw material for new stars. We then discuss real-time satellite tracking, orbital mechanics, and two-line element sets in low Earth orbit. We also examine how corporate space weather services protect essential terrestrial and orbital infrastructure, and we unravel the gravitational secrets of dark matter holding galaxies together.
Finally, we cover today's key space events and daily highlight: the close pass of near-Earth asteroid 2025 UK9 happening today, September 4, 2026, and the upcoming weekend launch of NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Kennedy Space Centre.
For real-time dashboards, Kp updates, and interactive forecasts, visit https://flarient.com.
